description: Chat Demo
readme:
# chat-demo

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A static chat demo powered by the DeepSeek API. No application backend is required: the browser connects directly to the configured API service.

You can [try the app online](https://deepseek-ai.github.io/chat-demo/) or download the archive from [Releases](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-chat-demo/releases), extract it, and double-click `index.html` to use it locally without installation or a build. Enter your API key in Settings before your first chat.

## Getting started

Install Node.js 22.12+ and pnpm, then run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/chat-demo.git
cd chat-demo
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

Open http://localhost:8090.

To build the static site:

```sh
pnpm build
```

The output is written to `dist/`. Deploy it to a static web server or open `dist/index.html` directly. Opening the file directly requires browser support for storage on `file://` pages and an API service that permits their cross-origin requests.

## Features

- Multiple conversations with automatic titles, renaming, and deletion; edit prompts, regenerate replies, and switch between message branches.
- Streaming replies, deep thinking, smart search, link reading, and source citations; stop generation or continue eligible replies.
- Upload, paste, or drag and drop attachments; use voice input and read replies aloud. A live audio spectrum appears in the first row of the input area while recording on mobile.
- Markdown, syntax highlighting, KaTeX math, and Mermaid diagrams.
- Simplified Chinese and English, light and dark themes, mobile layouts, location settings, and chat history import and export.

## Data and storage

Your API key and settings are stored in the browser's localStorage. Conversations and original attachments are stored in IndexedDB. Local data is isolated by browser profile and site origin. Sending messages, uploading attachments, and using speech features sends the relevant content to the configured API serv

name: supermimic
description: Humanoid whole-body motion tracking with one differentiable world model.
readme:
# SuperMimic

[Project page](https://supermimic.github.io) | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28480)

SuperMimic trains a humanoid whole-body motion tracker with one differentiable world model, built on [mjlab](https://github.com/mujocolab/mjlab).

## Setup

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

Clone both repos as siblings:

```bash
mkdir supermimic_ws && cd supermimic_ws
git clone git@github.com:HybridRobotics/supermimic.git
git clone git@github.com:HybridRobotics/mjlab_research.git
cd supermimic
```

## Usage

Available task IDs:

- `SuperMimic-GenCoord-G1` — generalized coordinates representation
- `SuperMimic-MaxCoord-G1` — maximal coordinates representation

Train a world model and policy:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<GPU_ID> uv run src/supermimic/scripts/train.py \
  <TASK_ID> --runner.run_name <description>
```

Play back a trained model:

```bash
uv run src/supermimic/scripts/play.py \
  <TASK_ID> --wandb-path <RUN_PATH>
```

## Acknowledgements

SuperMimic contains code inspired by these projects:

- [ControlVAE](https://github.com/heyuanYao-pku/Control-VAE) (BSD-3-Clause)
- [robotic_world_model](https://github.com/leggedrobotics/robotic_world_model) (Apache-2.0)
- [DreamerV3](https://github.com/danijar/dreamerv3) (MIT)

## License

Copyright 2026 The SuperMimic Authors.

Released under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

readme:
# Abyssal Garden

**A dreamy underwater world you can swim through, right in your browser.**

Towering kelp forests, sunbeams pouring through a rippling surface, a sunken ship, manta rays gliding overhead.
And all of it is made by code: no images, no 3D models, no sound files. The whole world fits in **one 96 KB HTML file**.

![Kelp forest with a stone whale tail and a manta ray](.github/screenshots/whale-fluke.jpg)

## Try it

1. Download [`index.html`](index.html).
2. Open it in **Chrome** or **Edge** on a desktop computer.
3. Wait a few seconds while the world is built, then press **Dive in** and start swimming.

Nothing to install, and it works offline. It needs a browser with **WebGPU**. If you see *"This scene needs WebGPU"*, update your browser or switch to Chrome / Edge.

## What's down there

- **Kelp forests** that sway in the current and sparkle with tiny gold and green specks
- **Light rays** streaming down from a wavy surface, with shimmering caustics on the sea floor
- **A sunken wooden ship**, a **giant stone whale tail**, rock arches, canyons and floating boulders
- **Manta rays**, schools of fish, rising bubbles and drifting particles
- **A purple grotto** with glowing magenta ground cover, coral and barrel sponges
- **A soundscape** made up as you listen: a deep rumble, distant whale calls, soft chimes and bubbles

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Shipwreck](.github/screenshots/shipwreck.jpg) | ![Looking up through the kelp](.github/screenshots/kelp-forest.jpg) |
| ![Barrel sponges](.github/screenshots/sponge-garden.jpg) | ![Light rays over the kelp basin](.github/screenshots/light-rays.jpg) |

![The purple grotto](.github/screenshots/purple-grotto.jpg)

## Controls

| | Keyboard & mouse |
|---|---|
| Look around | Move the mouse |
| Swim | `W` `A` `S` `D` |
| Up / down | `E` / `Q` |
| Swim faster | Hold `Shift` |
| Jump to a viewpoint | `1` to `6` (the spots in the screenshots) |
| Menu | `Esc` releases the mouse and opens the menu with the list of controls; *

# muse.ai 注册 / 邀请码兑换 协议分析

补充一下，记得用JP 节点， JP 不需要绑卡，直接过

纯 HTTP 实现 muse.ai 的注册与邀请码兑换流程，不依赖浏览器。本文记录的是通过抓包逐字段比对得出的协议细节。

## 快速开始

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp config.example.json config.json   # 填入邮箱与可选代理
python example_register.py
```

## 目录结构

```
musepy/
  client.py    注册 + 兑换的完整协议客户端
  runner.py    多账号批量调度（sticky 代理 / 预算 / 停止语义）
  otp.py       验证码轮询（幂等：只取 send 之后的最新码）
  falco.py     行为埋点上报（可选）
  caa.py       注册漏斗事件上报（可选）
example_register.py        单账号端到端示例
example_batch.py           多账号批量示例
config.example.json        配置模板
test_onboarding_smoke.py   离线冒烟（披露解析纯函数）
test_runner_smoke.py       离线冒烟（批量调度，mock 网络）
```

## 协议流程

```
GET  /                                   拿初始 cookie
POST /api/auth/native/restart            → 201 {csrf_token}
POST /api/auth/native/send-otp           → 201
POST /api/auth/native/confirm-otp        → 200 {registration_state:"completion_required",
                                               tos:{content_version}}（动态 TOS 版本）
POST /api/auth/native/register-completion→ 200 {auth_meta_session:{frl_access_token, frl_account_id}}

     └ 从 muse.ai 文档解析动态披露 disclosure_text/disclosure_version 与状态门
       （resolvedDestination/isGeoGated/waitlist → 地区受限）
POST /api/hatch/accept-tos               → 200（单次调用；正文用服务端动态披露，非硬编码）
GET  /api/hatch/invite                   → 200 表示账号有效
POST /api/hatch/vm/wake                  → 200（必须，否则兑换误报 invalid；
                                             wake_trigger=mount + open_id + away_ms=0）
POST /api/hatch/stateful-sharing         → 200
POST /api/hatch/invite-code/redeem       → 200 {redemptionStatus:"redeemed"}
POST /api/hatch/invite                   → 200 {code}（取回自己的码，不等于页面刮开 reveal）
```

name: TelemetryCleaner
description: 基于 Shizuku 免 Root 清除国产安卓 SystemHelper、RegService 等系统预装隐私数据收集模块
readme:
# 遥测清理 · TelemetryCleaner > 运营商为终端入网、自注册、网络运维和故障排查，确有在相应场景收集必要数据的实际需求！本项目仅供学习，用于了解 Android 系统包管理机制。 TelemetryCleaner 可以检测国行 Android 固件预置的运营商组件，查看各空间的安装状态和权限，并管理卸载与恢复。下载： [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Eynnzerr/TelemetryCleaner/releases/latest)

您可通过不限于以下方式参与贡献，欢迎 PR： 1. 提供清单未覆盖的厂商+运营商+包名线索，在 README.md 中补充即可； 2. 提供针对某模块的实测与分析报告，不限制是否为 AI 生成，但需保证真实性。放于 docs 目录中即可； 3. 协助实现未支持的免 Root 卸载功能（如**现版本不支持部分 vivo 系的电信/移动组件卸载**）； 4. 对软件功能的反馈或改进。 ## 背景介绍 部分国产厂商在国行固件中预置了 `SystemHelper`、`RegService` 等运营商终端管理组件。这些组件在后台静默定时采集数据，用户无感；没有桌面入口，同时无法以常规手段禁用权限和卸载。 WiSec 2023 的流量测量还在部分国行样机上观察到运营商组件上报数据，其中小米及 ColorOS 样本的中国移动组件上报了已安装软件列表。 [WiSec 2023 实测论文](https://www.scss.tcd.ie/Doug.Leith/pubs/wisecfp034-liu.pdf#page=7) 在作者本人的 OPPO 真机上观测到 SystemHelper 有读取定位、设备和 SIM 标识、已安装应用以及按应用统计网络流量，随后向某云端上传的行为，分析详见 [SystemHelper 代码与权限分析 by AI](docs/systemhelper-analysis.md)。 ## 本项目原理 Android 10 及以上设备可安装本项目，依赖 Shizuku。先按 [Shizuku 启动指南](https://shizuku.rikka.app/guide/setup/)通过 ADB 或无线调试启动 Shizuku，再回到 App 授权并选择需要检查的空间。Android 11 及以上可用无线调试启动。检测完成后，可打开组件详情查看权限，或勾选组件批量操作。 ADB 启动的 Shizuku 以 shell 身份代理 Binder 调用。App 直接请求系统包管理服务，避开部分 ROM 对 `pm` 命令行入口的拦截。系统包管理服务仍会执行本机的权限和包状态校验。 [Binder 调用实现](app/src/main/java/com/eynnzerr/telemetrycleaner/data/PackageBinder.kt) 少数 ROM 会在命令层直接拒绝卸载系统应用，例如返回 `Failure [only root can delete system app for a particular user]`。收到这类系统错误后，App 会以 shell 身份通过 `app_process` 调用隐藏的 `IPackageManager.deletePackageAsUser` 再试一次；重新读取包状态确认失败后，结果页仍显示原始系统错误，不会用兜底流程的错误信息覆盖它。 [app_process 兜底实现](app/src/main/java/com/eynnzerr/telemetrycleaner/data/PackageFallback.kt) 卸载按选定空间执行，会清除该空间中的组件数据。恢复使用系统保留的 APK。自动清理默认关闭，开启后按配置的周期检查所选空间，只处理自动清理名单内的组件。 ## 内置组件清单 表中的「未验证」指尚无本人在相应厂商设备上的卸载验证。 | 厂商 | 运营商 | 包名 | 卸载验证 | | --- | --- | --- | -

# line-art-animation

A Claude skill and a small TypeScript library for animated line-art components:
ink-on-paper figures that walk, ride and react, in scenes that run from day to night.
Everything is drawn live in SVG, so it stays sharp at any size and responds to the
pointer.

![A Japanese street drawn in line art, going from late afternoon to night](media/village.gif)

| Day | Night |

readme:
# Relax

> [!WARNING]
> **Experimental, and not affiliated with Rust.** Relax, its compiler and its JIT included, is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Rust project or the Rust Foundation. It is an AI-generated reimplementation of the Rust language, designed to minimise latency for LLMs working with Rust code, and should be viewed only as an experimental developer tool. Rust is a trademark of the Rust Foundation.
>
> **It does not inherit Rust's safety guarantees automatically.** rustc's checks, and the memory safety they give safe code, hold under Relax only as far as Relax reimplements them correctly. Relax can contain any number of bugs at runtime, and a bug in Relax can make a correct program, safe code included, misbehave or crash.
>
> Relax is for development iteration: running, testing and live-editing your program while you work on it. Build anything you release with Rust itself: `cargo build --release` with rustc. So far it has been tested mostly in Makepad's own edit-run loop and only lightly on other projects, so expect rough edges elsewhere and please report them.

### Rust without the wait.

**rustc builds your program, then you run it. Relax runs your program while it builds it.**

Relax is a live compiler and JIT runtime for Rust, written in Rust. It runs a Cargo package straight
from source, with no rustc, LLVM or linker in the loop: it compiles each function when it is first
called, optimises the hot ones while the program runs, and patches your edits into the running process.

## Relax vs cargo and rustc

readme:
# ScanDot

[![CI](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

ScanDot is an experimental Android app for capturing and viewing 3D point clouds on a supported phone. It combines ARCore camera tracking and depth estimates, saves scans locally, and provides an interactive viewer.

The repository also contains a separate video photogrammetry pipeline that runs on a workstation using FFmpeg and COLMAP. **The Android app does not reconstruct ordinary video with photogrammetry on the phone.**

## Current status

- Capture, save and reopen point clouds on devices that support ARCore Depth.
- Rotate, pan and zoom scans in the viewer. An optional full-depth mode interpolates missing depth and can distort surfaces.
- Prepare video frames and run a sparse or dense COLMAP reconstruction on a workstation.

This is an early prototype. Results can contain gaps, drift and noise; they are not textured meshes or validated measurements. Reflective, transparent and textureless subjects are difficult. Capture quality and device compatibility need further testing.

## Try the preview

Download the [preview APK](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/releases/tag/v0.3.0-preview.1). The release notes describe compatibility and signing limitations.

## Build the Android app

You need JDK 17, Android SDK 36, and an Android device with ARCore Depth support. Camera permission is required; Google Play Services for AR may require installation or an update.

```sh
cd android-app
./gradlew assembleDebug lintDebug testDebugUnitTest
```

On Windows, use `gradlew.bat` in place of `./gradlew`. The debug APK is written to `android-app/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`. Install it as an update to preserve existing app data.

readme:
# gpucanvas

Put thousands of live DOM nodes on an infinite canvas: the GPU draws them, an editor selects,
moves and resizes them, shaders and transitions run on them, and an AI agent can read them and
point at them.

![The same 5,000 live React screens as plain DOM (left) and in gpucanvas (right), with each side's frame rate measured live](docs/benchmark.gif)

The same session on both sides: 5,000 live React screens, the same camera path, a message typed and sent. Left, every screen is plain DOM under a CSS transform. Right, gpucanvas. Recorded in Chrome on a MacBook Pro; the frame rates are measured live in each run. Run it yourself in the [live demo](https://berkantay.github.io/gpucanvas/).

- **[Canvas](#how-it-works).** Live React or plain DOM nodes, drawn by WebGPU in one instanced
  pass. Pan and zoom never touch the DOM, and clicks, typing and state still reach the real
  elements.
- **[Editor](#editing).** Click to select, double-click to go a layer deeper, down to any element
  or React component. Move and resize with snapping guides.
- **[Shader effects](#shader-effects).** Run WGSL on live components: a glass lens, frost,
  shockwaves, glitch, VHS, or your own.
- **[Snapshots](#snapshots).** Any node as an image, pixel diffs between versions, and a
  filmstrip of its history.
- **[Agent view](#agent-view).** What is on the canvas as a short JSON tree with ids, and an
  image of any region, for an AI agent to read and point at.
- **[Transitions](#transitions).** Dissolve, wipe or fade a node out and another in, on the
  GPU, while both stay live.
- **[Marks](#marks).** Arrows between elements, comment pins, notes and live cursors that
  follow the camera.

![An agent cursor flags a heading, links two buttons and drops a pin; the screen wipes out and dissolves back; a glass lens follows the pointer; shockwaves ripple from clicks](docs/features.gif)

Marks from an agent, a wipe and a dissolve, the glass lens and shockwaves, all on live
components. Recorded

name: PeakCut
description: AI clipping for long videos and live streams. Self-hosted, bring your own AI key.
readme:
# PeakCut

Turn long videos and live streams into captioned vertical clips, ready to post. Free and open source: run it on
your own computer or server, with your own AI key.

Paste a YouTube, Twitch or Kick link (or upload a file) and PeakCut finds the moments worth clipping, cuts them to
9:16, adds word-by-word captions and a hook, and can post them to your connected accounts. It can also record a
creator's live stream and clip the highlights while the stream is still running.

## What it does

- **Clips from any video.** Transcribes the audio, asks an AI which moments would hold a stranger's attention, and
  renders each one with captions in one of three styles.
- **Live clipping.** Records a stream into a rolling buffer and clips as it happens, using loudness, chat activity
  and the transcript.
- **Workspaces per creator.** Channels, clip settings, posting rules and an activity log for each creator you clip.
- **Posting.** Connect YouTube, Instagram and TikTok in one click, then queue or auto-post finished clips, with
  spacing and daily caps (see [DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md#connecting-youtube-instagram-and-tiktok) for the one-time setup).
- **No sign-in on your own computer.** It opens straight into the dashboard. On a shared server, switch accounts on
  (`PEAKCUT_ACCOUNTS=1`) for email or Google sign-in and an admin dashboard.
- **Your own AI.** Gemini, OpenAI, Grok, Groq, OpenRouter, Claude, a local model through Ollama, or anything that
  speaks the OpenAI chat format. No key at all also works: clips are then picked by loudness.

## Quick start

You need Python 3.10 or newer and `ffmpeg`. On Windows: `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`. On a Mac: `brew install ffmpeg`.
On Linux: `sudo apt install ffmpeg`. PeakCut finds it by itself and tells you in the dashboard if it is missing.

```bash
git clone <this repository> peakcut
```

```bash
cd peakcut
```

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Start the server:

```bash
python -m studio.server
```

name: Haru
description: Haru: a low-latency, multilingual, full-duplex spoken dialogue model
readme:
# Haru [Model](https://huggingface.co/higurashi-ai/Haru-4B) · [Technical blog](https://blog.higurashi.ai/melte/haru4b/) · [Technical blog (Japanese)](https://blog.higurashi.ai/melte/haru4b-ja/) Haru is a low-latency and multilingual full-duplex spoken dialogue model: it listens and speaks at the same time, the way people do on a phone call. This repository contains the inference code for **Haru-4B**, a pretrained base model, with three implementations and a web demo. - **Native full-duplex at 7.5 Hz.** Every 133 ms the model takes one frame of the user's audio and produces one frame of its own audio and text. User audio, model audio and model text are summed into a single position of the language model, so listening and speaking never wait for each other. - **Continuous audio, one sampling step.** Audio is a 64-dimensional latent per frame. A small MLP head with MeanFlow sampling produces it in one step from the language model's hidden state; there is no separate audio transformer and there are no discrete audio tokens. - **Character and voice control.** A text card sets the character, a short reference clip sets the voice. - **Multilingual.** English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Chinese, Japanese, Russian and Korean. ## How it works

- The **text stream** carries the model's words in chunks. Frames without text hold a padding token, and an end-of-padding token on the frame before the model starts to speak. - The **audio codec** is the causal VibeVoice acoustic tokenizer: 24 kHz audio to and from one latent per 3200 samples. - The **prompt** is the character card as a system turn, followed by the voic

readme:
# SignDrop
## Windows Common Log FileSystem Authentication 0day Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

This vulnerability won't affect all windows machines but I guess estimate 80% of the world's windows installations are vulnerable to this.
To check, you need to run the proof of concept or check your registry configuration, if it spawns a SYSTEM shell, you're vulnerable. And you're generally vulnerable if your windows installation is older than 90 days so it's safe to assume that everyone reading this is definitely vulnerable.

You might ask why, it's because it depends if the CLFS authentication mitigation is enabled or not, it's because of this : 
- https://windowsforum.com/news/clfs-authentication-mitigation-in-windows-90-day-learn-mode-for-log-files.396323/
- https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/servicing/os/windows/2025/03/common-log-file-system-clfs-authentication-mitigation

From Microsoft :
> Currently, the adoption period lasts for 90 days, starting from the time in which the system was first started with this version of CLFS. After this 90-day adoption period has lapsed, the driver will automatically transition into enforcement mode on its next start, after which CLFS will expect all logfiles to contain valid authentication codes. Note that this 90-day value may change in the future.


Since October 28, 2025, Microsoft released the CLFS authentication mitigation in the official release channel to curb the exploitation of CLFS vulnerabilities since CLFS was an easy target to exploit since it parsed complex log files in kernel mode. So if anything goes wrong, it's a memory corruption that can be exploited to gain elevated privileges.
After the mitigation was implemented, there was a sharp decline in publicly exploited CLFS vulnerabilities since it no longer represented a massive attack surface but the mitigation introduced a new vulnerability that I'm calling "SignDrop"

The specific flaw exist in clfs.sys in the way how it handle the creation of the auth

name: tiny-voca
description: A 4.5M-parameter two-voice English text-to-speech model, trained from scratch
readme:
# tiny-voca

tiny-voca is a small English text-to-speech model. It has two voices, 4.5M
parameters, and runs on a CPU or in the browser.

[Demo](https://tiny-voca.n4ze3m.com) · [Weights](https://huggingface.co/n4ze3m/tiny-voca) · [Dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/n4ze3m/tiny-voca)

## Features

- **Small**: 4,537,291 parameters, 18 MB, waveform generator included.
- **Fast**: about 70x real time on four CPU threads.
- **Two voices**: F2 (female) and M2 (male), American English, 24 kHz.
- **Runs anywhere**: PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime Web.
- **Open**: code, weights, training recipe and dataset. Trained from scratch.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/n4ze3m/tiny-voca.git
cd tiny-voca
pip install -e ".[own]"
hf download n4ze3m/tiny-voca --local-dir weights
export DIZIONE_DATA=weights/phonemizer
```

## Usage

```bash
python -m tiny_voca.infer \
  --checkpoint weights/tiny-voca.pt \
  --voice F2 \
  --text "Hello! This is tiny voca." \
  --output hello.wav
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--text-file` | | Read the text from a file instead of `--text` |
| `--voice` | `F2` | `F2` or `M2` |
| `--speed` | 1.0 | Speaking rate |
| `--pitch-shift` | 0 | Raise or lower the pitch |
| `--pitch-range` | 1.0 | More or less pitch movement |

Long text is fine. It is read one sentence at a time and the audio is joined.
A text that ends without a mark gets a full stop, so the last word does not
break off. A sentence with nothing to read, such as one in another script, is
skipped. The output never peaks above 0.99, so it does not clip as a 16-bit
WAV. In Python, `tiny_voca.infer.speak_text` does the same.

## ONNX

```bash
python -m tiny_voca.export --checkpoint weights/tiny-voca.pt --output tiny-voca.onnx
```

A ready file is in the weights repository as `onnx/model.onnx`. The
[model card](https://huggingface.co/n4ze3m/tiny-voca) shows how to call it.

name: Videohub
readme:
# VideoHub

**A local review studio and render queue for videos that Claude Code or OpenCode writes as code.**
Ask your agent for a video. It builds a film as a web page that draws every frame in code. VideoHub plays the film straight from its code, so you can watch it, step through frames, draw and leave notes before rendering. Send the notes back to your agent, review the fixes in the reloading preview, then render when you are ready. The queue keeps the computer usable and can re-render only the seconds that changed.

> **Windows 10/11, Linux and macOS; Claude Code or OpenCode. Linux and macOS are new, not yet tested on real machines.** See [platform support](docs/PLATFORMS.md) for feature limits and the remaining hardware checks.

![Live preview with a note on a frame](docs/screenshots/review-live-preview.png)

## Features
- **Projects** — every film in your watched folders with its videos, versions, notes and disk use; a live cover for
  films that have no video yet.
- **Live preview, no render** — plays a film from its page (`window.renderOut(t)`), frame-accurate, with its sound,
  scenes and narration on a timeline. Changing the code reloads the open preview in place.
- **Review notes** — click or draw on any frame (or pick a frame range), type what is wrong. **Send to Claude / OpenCode** (Settings → Agent name) copies
  a short message; your agent reads the notes (time, frame, chunk, a close-up picture of your drawing) with `hub_notes`.
- **Check fixes** — a tour through the notes your agent marked fixed, with before/after; "Still there" sends one back.
- **Render queue** — one render at a time on the PC, waits for renders started elsewhere, progress and ETA, a
  render dialog with size/fps/workers/encoder, a copy to any folder, a desktop notification when available.
- **Partial re-render** — a film rendered in 2-second chunks re-renders only the chunks your notes touched, joins the
  film again and saves `film_vN.mp4` with the changed ranges; **Watch only t

name: kraken-mount
description: Minimalist PS5 game mounter supporting PKG, folder dumps, zstd and lz4
readme: A PS5 game mounter. It finds games on the internal SSD, the M.2 drive and USB drives, and adds them to the home screen without installing them. Supported formats: debug FPKG (`.pkg`) and game folders (plain, or packed with zstd or LZ4). Other formats, such as exFAT images, are obsolete and will not be supported. ## How to 1. Download `kraken-mount.elf` from [Releases](https://github.com/quer3q/kraken-mount/releases) and send it to your jailbroken PS5 with the ELF loader (elfldr, port 9021) or payload-manager: `nc -w 3 9021 < kraken-mount.elf`. kstuff must be loaded, and ShadowMount+ must not be running: Kraken Mount waits until both are true. 2. Put each game in a scan root: - internal SSD: `/data/homebrew`, `/data/etaHEN/games` - M.2 or extended drive (`/mnt/ext0`, `/mnt/ext1`): `homebrew`, `etaHEN/games` or the drive root - USB drive (`/mnt/usb0` to `/mnt/usb7`): `homebrew`, `etaHEN/games` or the drive root 3. Each game gets a " registered" notification and its own home-screen tile. [ampr-emu-ng](https://github.com/quer3q/ampr-emu-ng) comes bundled and is installed into `/data/krakenmount/ampr/` at start. To run another build, put its `libSceAmpr.sprx` there; it is kept until you delete it. Caches live in `/data/krakenmount/caches/`, settings in `/data/krakenmount/config.toml` and the log in `/data/krakenmount/kraken.log`. To build it yourself: `ps5/build.sh` (needs Docker), output `target/ps5/kraken-mount.elf`. ## Thanks - [drakmor/ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus): home-screen registration, the fakelib sandbox overlay and backports are ported from it. - [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk): the PS5 toolchain. ## License GPL-3.0-or-later (`LICENSE`). Third-party notices are in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`.

readme:
# Yab

Yet another browser. A small, quiet browser for the Mac, with an app for iPhone.

![Yab with tabs down the left, a product page, and an agent watching its price](docs/images/readme/window.jpg)

Yab is a browser with nothing in the way: a row of tabs, across the top or down the left, and the page. One field takes addresses and searches. Pages run on **WebKit**, the engine inside every Mac, or, on Apple silicon, on **Chromium**, per tab or per site. Agents from the AI providers you already pay for can work in tabs of their own, and never see a private tab.

**[Download Yab](https://yetanotherbrowser.com)** · macOS 15.4 or later · [What's new](https://yetanotherbrowser.com/changelog) · [Manual](https://yetanotherbrowser.com/manual)

## What it does

- **One field.** Type an address and you go there; type words and you search. It finishes addresses from your own history and sends nothing until you press Return.
- **Tabs that stay out of the way.** Pins, folders and spaces. Tabs from your last session come back instantly and cost nothing until you click them. `⌘K` finds any open tab.
- **Two engines.** WebKit by default; Chromium on Apple silicon for the sites that need it, with Chrome extensions, Chrome DevTools and the Chrome Web Store.
- **Blocking and hiding built in.** An ad blocker that runs inside the engine, before a request is made. `⇧⌘H` hides any element on a site, for good.
- **Reading mode, floating video, split view, Peek**, each one key away.
- **Passwords in your keychain**, or in the password manager you already use.
- **Agents in their own tabs**, with your sign-ins, asking before they send, pay or delete.
- **Sync that can't be read**: optional, end to end encrypted, between your Macs and iPhone.

![Reading mode in four themes](docs/images/readme/reading.jpg)

What Yab keeps and sends, line by line: [docs/privacy.md](docs/privacy.md). Every shortcut: [docs/keyboard.md](docs/keyboard.md).

Then I found Fury. Its open source gave me a starting point I could build on, and that's how PiBrowse began. **The open-source edition will always be free to download, use locally, and self-host.** PiBrowse Cloud is a separate, optional paid hosting service for teams and is still in development. — Aron ## Getting started macOS (Apple Silicon): [PiBrowse 0.5.5 preview](https://github.com/aronhy/pibrowse/releases/tag/v0.5.5). - **[Download desktop app for macOS (.dmg)](https://github.com/aronhy/pibrowse/releases/download/v0.5.5/pibrowse-0.5.5-macos-arm64.dmg)** - **[Download Chromium 157 core (.tar.xz)](https://github.com/aronhy/pibrowse/releases/download/v0.5.5/pibrowse-core-0.5.5-macos-arm64.tar.xz)** - [SHA-256 checksums](https://github.com/aronhy/pibrowse/releases/download/v0.5.5/SHA256SUMS.txt) The desktop app and rebuilt Chromium **157.0.8103.39** core are separate downloads. description: 歸藏 Game Skill：让 AI 从零做出能在浏览器里玩的 3D 动作游戏，附可玩演示《雾锁山门》。Agent skill for Claude Code / Codex that builds a playable browser 3D action game with AI-generated assets (three.js, single-HTML). Playable demo included.
readme:
# 歸藏 Game Skill **让 AI 从零做出一个能在浏览器里玩的 3D 动作游戏** [English](README.en.md) · 简体中文 [![试玩演示](https://img.shields.io/badge/试玩演示-雾锁山门-c9a45c?style=for-the-badge)](https://op7418.github.io/guizang-game-skill/) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL--3.0-blue?style=for-the-badge)](LICENSE) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/op7418/guizang-game-skill?style=for-the-badge&color=e9dcae)](https://github.com/op7418/guizang-game-skill/stargazers) *上面这段是演示游戏《雾锁山门》里的实机画面。[点这里直接玩](https://op7418.github.io/guizang-game-skill/)，电脑和手机都能打开，不用安装。*
--- ## 这是什么 一个给 AI 编程助手（Claude Code、Codex 等）用的 Skill。装上之后，对它说"做一个武侠题材的俯视角 3D 动作游戏"，它会按一套走通过的流程去做：先问清楚你要什么，接上你手头的素材生成工具，自己推进画面、自己截图核对，最后把游戏打包成一个网页文件。 Skill 里写的不是理论，是我用 Fable 5.2 花一个下午做出《雾锁山门》的过程中踩过的坑，和最后留下来的做法。那次大约 6 小时、4.5 亿 Token（其中一部分是 Opus 5.5 跑的测试），很多都花在了返工和试错上。这个 Skill 的目的就是让你和你的 AI 少走这些弯路。 ## 演示游戏：雾锁山门
一个仙侠题材的俯视角 3D 动作游戏：一个场景、一段小怪遭遇战、一场 Boss 战，有剧情和配音。**所有创意都是 AI 自己定的**，我只说了要做国风仙侠。 - **画面**：大片随风起伏的草，分层的雾、雪和远山，覆水石台上的反光。渲染流程是在 three.js 上自己搭的，只用兼容性最好的 WebGL，所以手机、电脑、小程序类容器里都能跑 - **角色与场景**：5 个带骨骼的 3D 角色、2 把武器、12 种场景道具、5 种掉落物。先用即梦出设定图，再用 Tripo 转成模型，提示词都是 AI 自己写的 - **战斗**：三段连招、闪避、格挡、弹反、处决，还有饮药、御剑和大招"万剑归宗"。Boss 有二阶段、起身过场和台词 - **声音**：8 条配音、配乐、环境音和音效 - **体积**：原始素材将近 100MB，打包后是一个约 33MB 的 HTML，里面包含全部模型、贴图、音乐和配音
三段连招 剑诀 万剑归宗
演示的三种形态，都是同一份源码打出来的： | 形态 | 说明 | |---|---| | [在线版](https://op7418.github.io/guizang-game-skill/) | 先渲染出场景再边跑边加载；手机有触屏摇杆和按钮；设置里可以调画质、换高清材质、改按键 |

The bundle is built to be deployed without a live network connection and ships with its runtime dependencies resolved ahead of time. It is maintained as an independent packaging effort, not as an upstream release. The deployment audience is administrators and power users who run air-gapped workstations, bandwidth-constrained environments, or reproducible lab images. Offline deployment matters here because the distribution can be staged on removable media, hashed once, and redeployed identically across many hosts without re-downloading. This keeps installs deterministic and auditable. The build covers both portable and installed modes from a single package, and it bundles the feature surface expected for the Discord Nitro Pro on Windows workflow. A single Discord Nitro Pro on Windows deployment covers both portable and installed modes, which simplifies staging. ## 01 · ⬇️ Download

readme:
# sakurai-skill YouTube「[桜井政博のゲーム作るには](https://www.youtube.com/@sora_sakurai_jp)」の**全本編257本の字幕**から作った、ゲーム制作の原則をまとめた Agent Skill（Claude Code などで使える `SKILL.md`）です。 ゲームの企画・ゲーム性・難易度・ご褒美・導入・操作感（ヒットストップ、ジャンプ、カメラ）・モーション・エフェクト・グラフィック・UI・サウンド・パラメーター調整・デバッグ・チーム運営・企画書・広報を考えるとき、レビューするとき、「手応えがない」「もっさり」と言われて直すときに使います。 > 非公式のファンメイドです。桜井政博氏・有限会社ソラとは関係ありません。中身は動画の内容を AI が要約したもので、桜井氏の発言そのものではありません。正確な内容は元の動画で確かめてください。 ## まずは動画で **[X の紹介ポスト](https://x.com/MvKWt5XpPV36233/status/2120977715864252887)** に、使い方の動画（約100秒）を付けています。このスキルで何ができるか（入れ方・頼み方・手ごたえの足し方・別のAIによるレビュー・レベルデザインの見直しなど）が、作例のゲームと一緒に見られるので、先に見ておくと分かりやすいです。 ## 入れ方 ```bash git clone https://github.com/kociden/sakurai-skill.git cp -r sakurai-skill/skills/sakurai ~/.claude/skills/ ``` Claude Code では「桜井さんならどうする？」「このゲームの手応えをレビューして」などと頼むと読み込まれます。 ## 作例：ハジキ このスキルを読み込んだ AI エージェントが、企画から磨き込み・タイトル・アイコンまで作った Godot 4.6 の一画面アクションです。敵の弾を引きつけるほど強く打ち返せます。 - [unityroom で遊ぶ](https://unityroom.com/games/hajiki) - [このゲームでスキルのどこを参照したか（動画番号つき）](examples/hajiki/README.md)
## 中身 ``` skills/sakurai/ SKILL.md 原則の要約（14章）と、レビュー・企画・手応えの直しの手順 references/ 動画ごとの要点をカテゴリ別に並べたもの（必要なときだけ読む） gameplay.md planning.md concepts.md specs.md motion.md effects.md graphics.md ui.md sound.md tech.md team.md mindset.md pr.md misc.md tools/ to_text.py 字幕（srv1）を時刻なしの本文にする build_refs.py 要点メモをカテゴリ別の references/ に並べ替える ``` - `SKILL.md` は約2.7万字。読み込みを軽くするため、具体的な数値・手順・作品例は `references/` に分け、必要なカテゴリだけを読む作りです。 - 各要点には動画の通し番号（古い順の 001〜259）とタイトルを付けているので、元の動画をたどれます。 ## 既存の Sakurai-Skills との違い 同じチャンネルを元にしたスキルに [kokuren333/Sakurai-Skills](https://github.com/kokuren333/Sakurai-Skills) があります（このリポジトリより先に公開されています）。目的は近いですが、作り方と向きが違います。 | | kokuren333/Sakurai-Skills | このリポジトリ | |---|---|---| | 元にした物 | まとめ動画（雑談を除く）を Gemini が要約した中間メモ。README によると動画との照合はしていない | 全本編257本の自動字幕を直接取得して要約 | | 範囲 | 原則177件＋横断原則17件 | 動画257本すべて（雑談回も `misc.md`

name: saltline-fable-5.2
readme: # Saltline — Fable 5.2 FPS A small browser first-person shooter: one level in a rainy container port. Cut three uplink relays while drones ("Gulls") and robot dogs ("Hounds") hunt you. ## Demo https://realcodebear.github.io/saltline-fable-5.2/ ## Where it comes from - Built by **Claude Fable 5.2**. The run was set up by Felix Rieseberg (Anthropic) and shared on X on 2026-11-09: https://x.com/felixrieseberg/status/2119925633564463609 - Original playable artifact: https://claude.ai/artifact/BGY1SztrAYcJQHSsnHHGmp - Per his post: one prompt, no human feedback, about 8 hours, about 2.7M output and 445M input tokens (heavily cached), about $550 at API pricing. Models, sounds and textures are all made in code. These numbers are his own and not checked here. All credit for the game goes to its original author. This repo is a mirror so people can run it locally. If you are the author and want it taken down, open an issue. ## What changed from the artifact Nothing in the game code. The claude.ai frame-runtime scripts were removed from ``, and a doctype, charset and viewport tag were added so the file runs as a plain web page. ## Run it ```sh python3 -m http.server 8731 ``` Then open http://localhost:8731 and click the page to capture the mouse and start the sound. The whole game is one file, `index.html` (~1.4 MB). It bundles three.js and loads fonts from Google Fonts. There are no other outside assets.

readme:
# CAPRI ### Your personal desktop AI agent. Built for Night City, runs on your PC. A local-first desktop agent with a cyberpunk soul. Capri sits on your machine, understands your intent, and executes: files, apps, browser, terminal, code. Plug in Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity or any other model backend and let it work.
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Outpostkrewhirl86/capri-ai?style=for-the-badge&color=f5e90a&labelColor=0b0b0f)](https://github.com/Outpostkrewhirl86/capri-ai/releases/latest) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Outpostkrewhirl86/capri-ai?style=for-the-badge&color=ff2a6d&labelColor=0b0b0f)](https://github.com/Outpostkrewhirl86/capri-ai/stargazers) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%2010%20%7C%2011-blue?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0b0b0f)](#installation) [![Build](https://img.shields.io/badge/build-portable%20ZIP-9d4edd?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0b0b0f)](#installation) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Outpostkrewhirl86/capri-ai?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0b0b0f)](LICENSE) [**Download for Windows**](https://github.com/Outpostkrewhirl86/capri-ai/releases/latest)  |  [Features](#features)  |  [Architecture](#architecture)  |  [Roadmap](#roadmap)  |  [FAQ](#faq)
--- ## What is Capri Capri is an open desktop AI agent inspired by the aesthetics and ideas of the **Cyberpunk: Edgerunners** universe: a fast, sharp, always-on netrunner assistant that lives on your machine instead of a browser tab. Most AI tools stop at a chat window. Capri goes further. It is an **agent runtime with a native desktop shell**: it receives a goal in natural language, plans the steps, calls tools on your system, observes the results, and iterates until the job is done. Think of it as your own Jarvis, only with a neon HUD and a much better soundtrack. Capri is model-agnostic. It wraps the coding and reasoning agents

name: pear
description: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
readme:
a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics

| Blog | Paper | Model | Documentation |

--- ## About PEAR is a post-training engine for agentic robotics: it trains reasoning models to natively use robots, with reinforcement learning in simulation. PEAR is the training infrastructure behind [Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots](https://mit-han-lab.github.io/pear-blog/), where an open 27B reasoning model learns to use real robots entirely in simulation, with zero demonstrations. PEAR trains with: - Fully asynchronous RL on [veRL](https://github.com/volcengine/verl) - GRPO, dynamic sampling, and Score Centering - FSDP and sequence parallelism for long-context training - Memory-efficient training with gradient checkpointing and activation offloading - Prefix caching across rounds, with [LMCache](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache) offloading the KV cache to CPU memory - Optimized kernels for H100, H200 and GB300 - Simulators on the same Ray cluster: MuJoCo on CPUs, Isaac Sim on GPUs PEAR evaluates with: - Robotic benchmarks: LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, LIBERO-Pro, RoboDojo and RoboLab-120 - General benchmarks: nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks through [EvalScope](https://github.com/modelscope/evalscope) PEAR deploys with: - A [model server](examples/models/qwen3_8_27b_pear/deploy/README.md): vLLM server on one RTX 5090 or GB300, with decode megakernels - A [robot station](examples/models/qwen3_8_27b_pear/deploy/README.md#drive-a-ro

description: A native Windows PC port of Super Mario Odyssey by static recompilation. Bring your own game: no game files included.
readme:
# Super Odyssey PC Recomp

A native PC port of Super Mario Odyssey for Windows and Linux, made by static recompilation - from your own copy of the game.

> [!NOTE] > **This is an AI-made project.** The code of this port was written by AI: almost all of it by **Claude** > (Anthropic's AI model, through Claude Code), with some fixes and features from OpenAI's **Codex**. The maintainer > doesn't write the code; they direct the work, test every build on Windows and a Steam Deck, and run the releases. > See [Who made this](#who-made-this). > [!IMPORTANT] > **You must bring your own game.** This project contains **no game files, no game code and no assets** - > only the installer and the source code. To play, you need the **`exefs` and `romfs` folders of your own copy of > Super Mario Odyssey**, already extracted. Instructions for getting game files are > not provided, and requests for game files will be closed. > [!WARNING] > **This is an early preview.** The whole game can be played, but there are known issues (see > [Known issues](#known-issues)) and things that still need fixing. Please report what you find. ## Current focus Updates will come **more slowly** for a while: the maintainer works a day job and has limited time, but the project continues. The order of work: 1. **The same as on the Switch, at 60 FPS.** Every kingdom compared with the Switch version (recordings and captures, side by side): rendering, effects, shadows, behaviour and timing. Any difference gets fixed, so that the port plays and looks 1:1 with the original. 2. **No stutter.** The shader preparation is being reworked to cover everything the game draws, to finish faster and to take far less disk space, so a first visit to a kingdom or effect never hitches. Smooth, stable frame pacing matters more here than higher numbers. 3. **The open [issues](../../issues)**

name: legwork-osint-ai-investigator
description: AI OSINT investigator for Windows: ask a question in plain words and get an answer built from public sources, with a source on every sentence.
readme:
Legwork: OSINT AI investigator that cites its sources

You ask. It does the legwork.
An AI investigator that answers with a source on every sentence.

OSINT · OSINT tool · AI investigator · AI agent · LLM · research assistant · citations · investigation · windows

> **Status: v1.2.1.** The app is out — [download Legwork for Windows](https://awesomeosint.tools/legwork/). ## Why this exists Every investigation starts the same way: twenty tabs, a notepad, and a question that keeps growing arms. The tabs win, the question loses. ## Why it is different Search engines answer queries; Legwork answers questions. It reads the sources it finds and writes the answer with a citation on every sentence — so you can check it, not just trust it. ## The idea - **One object.** A highlighter: the phrase a source backs up gets marked, and the source sits in the margin next to it. - **One number.** How many public pages it read to write the answer. - **Colour.** Ink `#121114` and paper `#F4F1EC`. Highlighter pink `#FF85C0` marks what is sourced, and the download. - **The main feature.** No source, no sentence: every line of an answer carries the public pages it came from, single-source claims are left out, and gaps are stated instead of guessed. ![Five steps as a trail of shoe prints with the counts for the sample question, then the three rules with a specimen beside each](docs/features.png) ## The demo on the page The question types itself in, the page count runs up, and the answer is written one line at a time: the key phrase gets the highlighter, each sentence carries numbered source chips, and the sources line up as cards under

name: MACaQ
description: SOTA model-agnostic quantization for GGUF, local inference and beyond. Quantize and run text, image, video and audio models with llama.cpp, vLLM, Diffusers and PyTorch.
readme:
![MACaQ: Model Agnostic Calibrated Quantization](docs/assets/macaq-banner.png)

**High-quality GGUF for local inference. Model-agnostic quantization beyond text.** Quantize and run text, image, video and audio models with llama.cpp, vLLM, Diffusers and PyTorch. MACaQ can quantize a **122B-parameter model in 64 minutes using just 32.5 GB of device memory**. You can get lower perplexity than MR-GPTQ and DuQuant++, or match their best Llama-3-8B perplexity with **11× less quantization time**. [Read the paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10649). **We also release [MACaQ-R](#macaq-r-with-standard-llamacpp) to refine existing GGUF models, improve their quality and adapt them to your workload, while keeping compatibility with standard llama.cpp.** Whether you’re a human or an AI agent, if you use MACaQ to quantize a model, please star [this repository](https://github.com/huawei-csl/MACaQ) to support the project. **Contents** - [Choose your backend](#choose-your-backend) - [Diffusers](#diffusers) - [llama.cpp](#llamacpp) - [MACaQ-R with standard llama.cpp](#macaq-r-with-standard-llamacpp) - [vLLM](#vllm) - [PyTorch](#pytorch) - [Ascend](#ascend) - [Citation](#citation) - [License](#license) ## Choose your backend - **[Diffusers](diffusers/README.md)**: image, video and audio generation, W4A4. - **[llama.cpp](llamacpp/README.md)**: text generation, 2/3/4-bit GGUF. - **[vLLM](vllm/README.md)**: text generation and serving, W4A4 or weight-only. - **[PyTorch](pytorch/README.md)**: speech generation, W4A

name: crate-ios
description: crate: run Linux VMs on iPhone and iPad
readme:
crate

Compact Runtime for Arm64 Translation and Emulation

Full Linux distributions, desktop and all, running in virtual machines on your iPhone and iPad, entirely on the device.

Ubuntu with GNOME, landscape on an iPhone Duo.

## Why crate - **A real computer in your pocket.** Not a remote desktop or a cloud VM: the whole operating system runs on the iPhone, works offline, and your files stay on it. - **Real distributions.** Stock arm64 Linux with its own package manager, so the software you'd run on an Arm laptop or server installs as it is: a browser, developer tools, coding agents like Claude Code, CAD apps. - **Built for speed.** We built crate to be fast, from the engine up. The [crate engine](https://github.com/oneamendez/crate) is written from scratch in Rust: an arm64-to-arm64 translator that copies most guest instructions into host code as they are and rewrites only what touches the machine. On a Mac, a benchmark pass that takes QEMU's TCG 130.5 s takes crate 24.5 s; the rest of the timings, the iPhone's included, are in the engine's [benchmarks](https://github.com/oneamendez/crate#benchmarks). - **GPU-accelerated.** The guest's OpenGL runs on the iPhone's GPU, through virglrenderer, ANGLE and MoltenVK: desktops composite in hardware, and 3D apps render on it. - **Made for the phone.** Touch is a tablet, a key row above the keyboard adds Esc, Ctrl, Super, Tab, function keys and arrows, the desktop follows the phone as it turns or folds, and iPhone Duo gets layouts of its own. ## What it runs Linux

readme: # Scarlet Scarlet is an open-source AI video editor for macOS, Windows and Linux. Tell Claude Code or Codex what you want to change, by voice or in writing, then play the edit on your timeline. Your original footage stays intact. Scarlet works especially well on dialogue-heavy recordings. Start with an interview, a video podcast or a talking-head take. Ask it to shorten long pauses, remove a repeated phrase or keep the clearest take of an answer. Tell it where the timing matters to you, such as a pause before a punchline. > “Tighten the pause before ‘three things.’ Let me hear it both ways.” Scarlet renders just the affected section so you can hear what a change sounds like in context. Requested edits go on the working timeline. Suggestions wait for you to apply them. For a first cut of a whole interview, you can jump straight to the cuts the agent flags for a second listen. [Download Early Access for macOS or Windows](https://github.com/Forward-Future/scarlet-releases/releases) · [Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64 preview](https://github.com/Forward-Future/scarlet-releases/releases?q=Ubuntu) · [Stable releases](https://github.com/Forward-Future/scarlet/releases) ## Run from source Scarlet is in early development. name: kaihen
description: Homebrew enabler and minimal CFW for Switch 2
readme:
# kaiHEN改変

kaiHEN改変 is a homebrew environment and minimal custom firmware for Switch 2.

## Warning

It's still a work in progress, and might have bugs.

We allow full access to the system, including the system NAND. A malicious
homebrew might write to your Switch 2 and brick it forever, so be warned.

## Components

- `ro/`: an `ldr:ro` service. It maps NROs into its clients' processes,
  publishes JIT code for them, and gives initialized clients a session with
  HEN.
- `bootstrap/`: the startup program. It starts HEN and the plugins, hands
  them the sessions they keep, and connects RO to HEN.
- `hen/`: HEN service. It starts the homebrew loader when a
  native game is opened with R held, gives each program its own session on
  an SM proxy, and serves the homebrew interface. See `hen/README.md`.
- `libkaihen/`: kaiHEN's homebrew API, with added JIT support.
- `common/`: code and protocol definitions.

## Starting it

HEN is started from various acquisition tools available for Switch 2. Run a
native game by holding R. The second launch and onwards will launch into
hbmenu.

## Developing homebrew

See the devkit repository,
[ouncebrew/ounce-devkit](https://github.com/ouncebrew/ounce-devkit), to
build homebrew. Existing Switch 1 homebrew that uses libnx and OpenGL or
Vulkan can be compiled for Switch 2 with it.

Homebrew and plugins are allowed access to all system modules fs can access,
so a large number of them.

## Building

With the Switch 2 devkit installed in devkitPro (see the devkit repository,
ouncebrew/ounce-devkit):

```sh
make
```

This builds RO (`ro/build/main`), HEN (`hen/build/main`), the bootstrap
(`bootstrap/build/bootstrap.bin`) and libkaihen (`libkaihen/build/`).
`make LIBOUNCE=DIR` can build against another libounce.

With Docker (or Podman), in the devkit's image.

```sh
docker build --output out .
```

writes `out/ro/main`, `out/hen/main`, `out/bootstrap.bin` and
`out/libkaihen/`.

```sh
docker build --build-arg RELEASE=1 --output out .
```

name: CarUp
readme:
# CarUp

CarUp 让 iPhone 通过有线或无线 CarPlay 连接安卓车机。连接后，可以在车机上使用 iPhone 的 CarPlay 应用，并在分屏仪表板上同时查看导航和控制音乐。

[下载 CarUp 4.0](https://github.com/nobcdz/CarUp/releases/download/v4.0/CarUp-4.0-release.apk) · [查看使用手册](使用手册/README.md)

**APK 来源说明**：本仓库通过 GitHub Releases 分享 APK。

![CarUp 首页，显示连接状态和无线、有线 CarPlay 入口](使用手册/images/home.webp)

## 先检测，再连接

打开 CarUp 的「检测」页，就能看到当前车机可用的连接方式。有线检测包含 **23 项**，无线检测包含 **37 项**。连接卡住时，可以在列表里查看进度停在 USB、蓝牙、Wi‑Fi、认证还是 iPhone 授权。

![车机能力检测，有线和无线 CarPlay 并列显示](使用手册/images/capability.webp)

| 连接方式 | 怎么开始 |
| --- | --- |
| 有线 CarPlay | 确认检测页显示 USB 主机可用，再用支持数据传输的线连接 iPhone。 |
| 无线 CarPlay | 在检测页确认无线条件就绪，从首页发起连接，按 iPhone 提示完成配对和授权。首次配对后可使用无线自动连接。 |

## 连接后的车机体验

在 CarPlay 中可以使用高德地图、汽水音乐等 iPhone 上支持 CarPlay 的应用。导航可以全屏显示，也可以切到仪表板，一边看路线和转向提示，一边控制音乐。

![CarPlay 仪表板，同时显示高德导航、下一步转向和音乐控制](使用手册/images/dashboard.webp)

| 音乐播放 | 全屏导航 |
| --- | --- |
| ![汽水音乐的播放页、封面和播放控制](使用手册/images/music.webp) | ![高德地图的车道转向提示和剩余路线](使用手册/images/navigation.webp) |

CarUp 提供自动画面适配、屏幕方向、音频缓冲、方向盘按键和浅色／深色外观等设置。进入 CarPlay 后，可从屏幕顶部双指下滑打开 CarUp 设置，或长按车机返回键回到 CarUp。

## 下载与安装

1. 打开 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/nobcdz/CarUp/releases/latest)，在 4.0 版本的附件中下载 `CarUp-4.0-release.apk`。
2. 将 APK 传到安卓车机，按车机提示完成安装。
3. 打开 CarUp，先到「检测」页确认可用的连接方式，再按[使用手册](使用手册/README.md)完成连接。

CarUp 的兼容目标为 **Android 4.0 及以上**。实际可用的连接方式取决于车机的 USB、蓝牙和 Wi‑Fi 能力，以设备上的检测结果为准。

readme: # xj-scanner Read the engine computer of a 1991–95 Jeep from a laptop, and let an AI agent do the reading. Three wires go from the diagnostic plug under the hood to a $3 Arduino Nano. The Nano plugs into your laptop over USB. From there Claude Code, Codex or any coding agent can read fault codes and live engine data, log a drive, and run the computer's built-in tests. It was built and tested on one car: a **1994 Jeep Cherokee XJ, 4.0L, engine computer 56030117**. Other 1991–95 Chrysler/Jeep computers of this family (SBEC, OBD1) should be close, but measure your own plug before you connect anything. ![Wiring: Nano D10, D11 and GND to cavities 4, 3 and 2 of the diagnostic plug](docs/img/wiring.svg) ## The easy way 1. Clone this repo and open it in Claude Code, Codex or another coding agent. 2. Say: **"Help me hook this up to my Jeep."** The agent reads [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and walks you through it one step at a time: the software, the breadboard, finding the right holes in the plug with a meter, and the first reading. Ask it to explain anything in simpler words. ## What you need (about $15) - Arduino Nano clone (5 V, USB-C or mini-USB) and its cable - Small breadboard and a few jumper wires - Three wires long enough to reach from the plug to where the laptop sits - Three 1/4" male spade terminals (they push into the plug) - A multimeter ## The one thing to get right **Cavity 6 is 12 volts with the key on. Never connect anything to it.** On the test car its wire is the same black/white as the ground wire, so don't go by color. Check every cavity with a meter first; [docs/connector.md](docs/connector.md) has the measurements to expect. ## Doing it by hand ```sh python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r pc/requirements.txt .venv/bin/python pc/xj_scan.py --cli DEMO # a simulated Jeep, to check your laptop side works brew instal

# Emissor de NFS-e Nacional

Emissor de NFS-e que fala direto com a API do Sistema Nacional NFS-e, sem intermediários e sem custo por nota. Ele roda
na sua conta da Cloudflare: o seu sistema envia os dados da venda e recebe a nota autorizada, com o XML, o PDF e links
prontos para mandar ao cliente.

Ele foi feito para empresas do Simples Nacional (ME, EPP e MEI) que prestam serviços no próprio município, e já emite
notas em produção para uma ME/EPP. Empresas fora do Simples ainda não são atendidas: veja
[para quem serve](#para-quem-serve).

## O que ele faz

- Emite a NFS-e e devolve o número, a chave de acesso e o XML autorizado.
- Nunca emite duas notas para a mesma venda: você escolhe o `id`, e repetir o pedido devolve a mesma nota.
- Se a resposta do governo se perder, ele confere se a nota foi emitida antes de enviar de novo.
- Cancela notas.
- Gera o PDF (DANFSe): usa o do governo quando o serviço dele responde; se não, gera um a partir do XML autorizado,
  com QR code para a consulta pública.
- Cria links assinados do PDF e do XML, que podem ir no e-mail do cliente.

Os testes validam os documentos contra os XSDs oficiais e conferem as assinaturas com o `xmlsec1`.

## Para quem serve

| Sua empresa | Funciona? | Em quais municípios |
|---|---|---|
| ME ou EPP do Simples Nacional | Sim. Já emite em produção. | Em todos os que têm o convênio ativo: 5.545 de 5.571, em 10/11/2026. |
| MEI | Sim, pelas regras oficiais. Ainda não foi testado em produção. | Em todos. |
| Fora do Simples (Lucro Presumido ou Lucro Real) | Ainda não. | — |

O emissor cobre o caso mais comum: serviço prestado no município da empresa, tributado pelo ISSQN e sem retenção. Veja
as [limitações](#limitações).

readme:
# PWMVID and GPU0 tools

This repository contains a PWMVID control-board design, STM32 firmware and host
tools, GA100 GPU0 register capture and analysis code, and an experiment-loop
description. Together they support board bring-up, PWM waveform experiments,
and checking how GPU register state changes after an attempt.

| Path | What it contains |
| --- | --- |
| [`hardware/`](hardware/README.md) | P8 KiCad schematic and PCB, test-pad map, and P9 assembly references |
| [`firmware/`](firmware/README.md) | STM32G431 application, custom USB bootloader, host utilities, and tests |
| [`driver/pwmvidctl/`](driver/pwmvidctl/README.md) | Operator CLI, sequence planner, calibration profiles, and waveform examples |
| [`gpu0-registers/`](gpu0-registers/README.md) | GA100 register maps, bounded capture engine, and offline state analysis |
| [`glitch-loop/`](glitch-loop/README.md) | Experiment-loop pseudocode and historical commanded waveforms |

## Offline checks

```sh
(cd firmware && sh tests/run_tests.sh && sh bootloader/tests/run_all.sh)
(cd driver/pwmvidctl && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v)
(cd gpu0-registers && cargo test --workspace --locked)
```

Building the STM32 images requires PlatformIO; see the firmware README for
build environments. Hardware bring-up requires the measurements in
[`firmware/docs/BENCH_ACCEPTANCE.md`](firmware/docs/BENCH_ACCEPTANCE.md).

Original project material is licensed under [MIT](LICENSE). Third-party terms
and source notices are described in [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md).

name: tinytraffic
description: self-host web analytics in a single binary
readme:
# tinytraffic

Simple, privacy-friendly web analytics for personal use. One binary, one
DuckDB file, no cookies.

- **Tracker**: ~1 KB gzipped. Pageviews (including SPA navigation), outbound
  link clicks and custom events. Accepts Plausible's event format, so existing
  Plausible integrations work.
- **Privacy**: no cookies or storage. Visitors are identified by
  `hash(daily salt, site, IP, user agent)`. The salt rotates at midnight in the
  site's timezone, and the IP is never stored. Referrers keep their domain and path; query strings are
  dropped.
- **Dashboard**: visitors, visits, pageviews, bounce rate and visit duration
  over time, plus sources, referrers, pages, locations, devices and goals.
  Click any row to filter. Light and dark themes, works on phones. Make a
  site's stats public to share its dashboard with anyone, no sign-in needed
  (rate limited to 300 requests a minute per IP).
- **API**: API keys for scripts and other apps. Read stats, manage sites, and
  send events from your server. See [docs/api.md](docs/api.md).
- **Stack**: Go + DuckDB backend. The dashboard is TanStack Start (SPA mode)
  with Solid and shadcn-style components, embedded in the binary.

## Quick start

With Docker:

```sh
docker run -d --name tinytraffic -p 8080:8080 -v tinytraffic:/data \
  -e TT_PASSWORD=change-me ghcr.io/egoist/tinytraffic:main
```

Behind a reverse proxy (Traefik, Caddy, nginx or Dokploy), add
`-e TT_TRUST_PROXY=true` and drop `-p 8080:8080`, so the proxy is the only way
in. Visitors are then located by their real IP. Without the flag, every visitor
appears to come from the proxy and shows as "Unknown", and viewers of public
dashboards share one rate limit. In Dokploy, add
`TT_TRUST_PROXY=true` under the app's Environment tab.

Or from source. You need [Go](https://go.dev) 1.26+, [Bun](https://bun.sh)
1.4+ and a C compiler (DuckDB is a C++ library, so the Go build uses cgo):

```sh
bun install                   # also fetches the GeoIP database
bun run

description: Solana validator health in 60 seconds: score, leader duties, rewards, disk forecast, Prometheus. One static binary, read-only, never touches your keys.
readme:
# Vigil

**Read-only, Alpenglow-aware Solana validator operations for Linux.**

Vigil combines the checks operators normally glue together: vote-account VAT runway, BLS registration, delinquency, identity consistency, leader production, per-slot missed duties, Prometheus metrics, Linux host audits, actionable alerts, and advisory maintenance planning.

[![CI](https://github.com/ValidatorStack/solana-vigil/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ValidatorStack/solana-vigil/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/ValidatorStack/solana-vigil)](https://github.com/ValidatorStack/solana-vigil/releases)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Go version](https://img.shields.io/badge/Go-1.23%2B-00ADD8)](go.mod)

> **Safety boundary:** Vigil never asks for a seed phrase, private key, or keypair file. It never signs or sends a transaction, changes host settings, restarts a validator, or switches identities. Use a local RPC and public validator addresses only. Test on testnet and with your own alert thresholds before production use.

## Production target: main Solana validator servers

Vigil is built to run **directly on Linux Solana mainnet-beta validator servers**—small, middle-sized, and large operators alike. It is not a laptop dashboard, an Ethereum tool, or a substitute for local validator observation. Run one Vigil instance on each validator server and point it at that server's local RPC and public vote account. An RPC-only node can expose compatible data, but host-audit and validator-duty results are meaningful only when Vigil runs on the actual validator being monitored.

The production target is mainnet-beta. Testnet remains supported as a staging environment so operators can validate configuration and alerts safely before a mainnet deployment; no source-code change or artificial network restriction is required. Linux AMD64 and ARM64 are the supported production platforms.

name: agweb
description: A browser built for agents - no focus stealing, a tiny footprint, all tabs in one view.
readme:
# agweb

A browser for coding agents on macOS, built on WebKit (Safari's engine). I run several coding agents at once, and Playwright's Chrome windows kept stealing my keyboard, while headless browsers got blocked by some sites and left me guessing what went wrong. agweb is one window that never takes focus: agents drive it from the shell with `agweb`, a playwright-cli-style command, and you watch them all live.

![The dashboard: every agent's tabs at once](docs/images/dashboard.png)

Idle tabs are suspended: on my Mac five open pages sit at 0% CPU, where Chrome's GPU process kept five to seven cores busy.

| Five idle pages   | Memory |
|-------------------|--------|
| agweb             | 590 MB |
| Headless Chrome   | 730 MB |
| Playwright Chrome | 1.6 GB |

- **Never steals focus.** No window comes to the front, nothing pops up. Dialogs, changing tabs, file pickers and downloads are answered in code.
- **You can always see it.** The dashboard (⌘D) shows every tab of every agent at once, live, with each agent's last command. And it is always a real window: some sites block headless browsers, and headless leaves you guessing what went wrong.
- **Many agents at once.** Each agent works in its own workspace with its own tabs, grouped by agent in the sidebar.
- **Log in once.** A named profile (`-p work`) keeps its logins and is shared by every agent using it, at the same time.
- **Light.** Idle tabs are throttled and then suspended, so open pages cost almost nothing once nobody uses them.
- **Acts like a person.** Clicks and keys are native macOS events, and the pointer moves like a hand, so hover menus and drag-and-drop work.
- **Made for agents.** Snapshots give each element a ref that lasts while it is on the page. `snapshot --diff` and `find` show only what matters, and every action reports what it changed.
- **Passwords stay out of the transcript.** `fill --secret-cmd 'pass show site'` types a secret the agent never sees in replies. 1Password and Bitwarden CLIs

readme:
# fastmint-fcfs

**English** · [Bahasa Indonesia](README.id.md)

**FCFS mint on BNB Smart Chain through Binance Agentic Wallet, landed in a block ±2 seconds after the sale opens.**

A skill for AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, and any other agent that reads `SKILL.md`) that fires a single mint/claim/buy transaction at the exact moment a sale opens, using a Binance Agentic Wallet (`baw` CLI). No private key on the machine: signing happens in Binance's backend through Developer Mode, the agent only prepares calldata and picks the moment.

```
sale opens (T)    T+0.05s          T+0.6–0.8s        T+1.3–1.5s       T+2.1–2.2s
   │                 │                  │                  │                 │
   ▼                 ▼                  ▼                  ▼                 ▼
 start ───► preview sent ───► simulation OK ───► BROADCASTED ───► in a block
         (NTP clock trigger)    (requestId)     (baw execute)     (receipt)
```

The numbers above were measured 11 Nov 2026 from Indonesia: 3 time-gated dry-runs plus one real mint (Pocket Moons, 2 free NFTs, trigger→receipt 2.0 seconds). The previous sequential version took 5–6 seconds.

---

## Table of contents

1. [How it works](#1-how-it-works)
2. [Installation](#2-installation)
3. [Usage flow](#3-usage-flow)
4. [Command reference](#4-command-reference)
5. [Dynamic arguments](#5-dynamic-arguments)
6. [Safety rails](#6-safety-rails)
7. [Measured numbers](#7-measured-numbers)
8. [Troubleshooting](#8-troubleshooting)
9. [File layout](#9-file-layout)
10. [FAQ](#10-faq)

---

## 1. How it works

### Why the old version was slow

`baw` has no direct-send command for a contract call. The flow is two steps by design: `contract-call preview` (the backend simulates and returns a `requestId`) and then `contract-call execute --requestId`. name: tradingview-indicator-for-ai-agents
description: Tradingview IndicatorBuilt for AI agents
readme:
# AI Agent Lens

**A TradingView indicator built for AI agents.**

Indicators were built for human eyes: colors, arrows, lines. An AI agent can't trade on colors. AI Agent Lens breaks down every closed candle into clean, structured JSON and sends it to any AI agent the moment the candle closes. Your agent reads the chart candle by candle, understands the context, and turns it into clear trading signals. You make the final call.

It works with any agent. It's built to shine with long-horizon reasoning models like **Claude Fable 5.2**.

Open source · MIT license · Pine Script v6 · No repainting

---

## What your agent receives on every candle

One JSON packet per closed candle with everything a trader looks at:

- **Candle breakdown:** body, wicks, range versus ATR, where it closed in its range, gap, pattern (engulfing, hammer, doji, inside bar and more)
- **The last 5 candles** in the same format, so the agent reads the sequence, not one bar
- **Regime:** `TREND_UP`, `TREND_DOWN`, `RANGE` or `HIGH_VOLATILITY`
- **Trend:** EMA 20/50/200 stack, 200 EMA slope, higher-timeframe bias
- **Momentum and strength:** RSI, MACD histogram, ADX, DI+ and DI-
- **Volume and volatility:** relative volume, ATR, ATR percentile
- **Structure:** swing highs and lows, breakouts and breakdowns
- **Levels:** previous day high and low, VWAP
- **Long and short scores (0 to 100)** with the five factors behind each score
- **Risk map:** entry, ATR stop, 1.5R and 3R targets, and live trade status

Full field list: [docs/PACKET_SCHEMA.md](docs/PACKET_SCHEMA.md) · Example: [examples/sample_packet.json](examples/sample_packet.json)

---

## How it works

```
 TradingView chart                 Your AI agent                    You
 ┌───────────────────┐  webhook   ┌──────────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐
 │  AI Agent Lens    │ ─────────► │ reads the JSON packet    │ ─► │ signal:      │
 │  closes a candle, │  JSON per  │ breaks down the candles  │    │ LONG / SHORT │
 │  builds a packet  │

# FableFlight ### An Open-World Flight Simulator Built in Pure Rust Explore the skies with real-world weather, live air traffic, and an immersive open-world flying experience. *Created with Claude Fable 5.2 & Opus 5.5*
[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/9akYzMRBc6) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-CE422B?style=for-the-badge&logo=rust&logoColor=white)](https://www.rust-lang.org/)
# Compiling * Install rust ``` cargo build --release ``` running ``` cargo run --release ``` # Language The interface is in English or French. It follows the system language, can be changed in Settings (start screen or pause menu), and is remembered. For one run: `cargo run --release -- --lang fr`. # Joysticks, pedals and key bindings Any joystick, throttle, rudder pedals or wheel can be used: in Bindings (pause menu, or Settings on the start screen), bind each axis by moving it the way that means "more" (nose up, right roll, right rudder, full throttle, brake pressed) and each button to any action. Everything is kept in `bindings.json` in the config folder. # Fuel and engine start The engines burn fuel as they work (the Cessna some 30 l/h at 75% power, the 747 about 10 t/h in the cruise) and the fuel weighs: full tanks fly heavier than empty ones. Choose how much to take on the start screen (Flight); the HUD, the flight panel (fuel, flow, endurance) and the cockpit gauges show what is left, with LOW FUEL / NO FUEL warnings, and a dry engine stop

readme:
# 桌面图标台球 · Desktop Icon Billiards

**把 Windows 桌面图标摆成一局台球。** 在桌面上移动鼠标瞄准，按住左键蓄力，松手击球。图标保留自己的缩略图，会滚动、碰撞和入袋。退出后，桌面恢复原样。

Windows 10 / 11 x64 · 单文件 EXE · MIT

![实机画面：桌面图标排成球阵，白球瞄准库边，虚线显示反弹路线](docs/images/desktop-gameplay.jpg)

## 下载

Windows 版 v0.2.4 为单文件 EXE。[GitHub 下载](https://github.com/liuxiaogang-com/desktop-icon-billiards/releases/download/v0.2.4/DesktopIconBilliards-0.2.4-win-x64.exe) · [CNB 国内镜像](https://cnb.cool/liuxiaogang/desktop-icon-billiards/-/releases/download/v0.2.4/DesktopIconBilliards-0.2.4-win-x64.exe)

`desktop-icon-billiards` 的源码和发布附件在两个平台同步。[GitHub 仓库](https://github.com/liuxiaogang-com/desktop-icon-billiards) · [CNB 国内镜像仓库](https://cnb.cool/liuxiaogang/desktop-icon-billiards)

官网入口为 [桌面图标台球](https://go.liuxiaogang.com/zmtq)。

## 玩法

1. 启动后等桌面图标摆好。移动鼠标选择白球的出球方向，**按住左键蓄力，松手击球**。按下的位置旁会显示「力度」进度条；力度在 0%～100% 之间往返循环，1.5 秒升满、1.5 秒降回零；进度条显示百分比和升降方向，松手按当前力度击球，轻点可小幅推球。
2. 用「**辅助线 · 开 / 关**」切换瞄准辅助。白线标记首次碰撞前的路线，蓝线表示白球碰球或碰库后的方向，绿线表示被撞图标的方向。待击球时即可查看方向，路线不随蓄力值变化，画到下一次碰撞或洞口；辅助线不代表实际滚动距离，能否到达仍取决于击球力度。辅助线带有描边，并会根据壁纸明暗自动换成深色或浅色，浅色壁纸上也看得清。路线上还会淡淡地画出碰撞圈：白球接触瞬间的位置，以及被撞图标的碰撞范围（比图标本身略大，这就是实际判定碰撞的圆）；图标被撞到时也会闪现一圈。
3. 主窗口显示本局用时、进球数和剩余图标数。白球入袋时会尝试自动摆回，如果没有合适的位置，可以点击台面空处摆球。白球入袋不计入进球数。
4. 清台后查看总用时和图标总数。点击「**重新开始**」重置本局，也可以在中途重开。
5. 点击「退出」、按 `Esc` 或使用全局快捷键 `Ctrl+Alt+X`，恢复桌面。

### 计时与全球排名

- 用时从**第一杆击出**算起，到最后一颗图标入袋为止，精确到毫秒。开球前的瞄准不计时。清台后会显示「本局平均 X 秒/颗」，也就是总用时除以图标总数。
- 球数固定在 **15～45 颗**。桌面图标少于 15 个时，复制现有图标补足到 15 颗；多于 45 个时只取其中 45 个，优先快捷方式和程序，其次是文件，文件夹排在最后，同类按桌面顺序取。主窗口会显示「桌面 N 个图标，复制补到 / 取其中 X 颗」。补球和落选的图标都只在游戏画面里生效，不会改动桌面，退出后照常恢复。
- 「全球排名」**默认关闭**。第一次启动会弹出一次询问，选「是」才开启，选「否」不会上传任何东西；之后可随时用主窗口的「排名」按钮开关。开启后，每局清台时提交一次成绩，用平均每颗用时排名。
- 开启排名需要联网，没有网络或服务不可用时游戏不受影响，只是这一局不计入排名。
- 每局清台后会弹出**成绩卡片**：游戏名与图标、段位（传奇球王、桌面球王、大师、高手、熟手、新秀）、全球名次和超过的玩家比例、用时、平均每颗用时、图标数、击球数和个人最佳，底部带有作者标记。点「保存图片」会存成 1080×1350 的 PNG（在「图片」文件夹的 `DesktopIconBilliards` 里），点「复制图片」可直接粘贴到微信、QQ 或帖子里。点击顶部「排行榜」或成绩窗口「查看排行榜」可查看全球前 50 条个人最佳成绩，自己的名次高亮并固定显示在底部。卡片只含成绩，不会出现你的桌面图标和文件名；没开启排名时卡片以平均每颗用时为主，并提示开启排名。

readme:
# shoji-bar-4

A Material 3 Expressive desktop shell for [ShojiWM](https://github.com/bea4dev/ShojiWM), written in Rust on [AntiWebUI](https://github.com/bea4dev/AntiWebUI).

![shoji-bar-4 on ShojiWM](./ss.png)

- **Top or vertical side bar** of floating islands: launcher, workspaces, the active window, a rolling clock, now playing, tray and status icons.
- **Dock** that hides at the bottom edge and rises when the pointer reaches it.
- **Quick settings**, **calendar**, **launcher**, **clipboard history**, **media player**, **notifications**, **OSD** and a **lock screen**.
- **Dynamic color** from a seed or the wallpaper, moved to on a spring everywhere at once, window frames included.
- Springs and shape morphs throughout, and no frames drawn while nothing moves (0% CPU when idle).

## Getting started

You need ShojiWM, a Rust toolchain, and the usual desktop services: NetworkManager, BlueZ, PipeWire, UPower, power-profiles-daemon and logind. `cliphist` and `wl-clipboard` give the clipboard history, and `zenity` lets you pick a user picture.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/bea4dev/shoji-bar-4 ~/.config/shoji-bar-4
cd ~/.config/shoji-bar-4
cargo build --release
```

ShojiWM's default config starts `~/.config/shoji-bar-4/target/release/shoji-bar-4` with the session, binds its keys (`Super` for the launcher, `Super+N` quick settings, `Super+C` calendar, `Super+V` clipboard, `Super+L` lock) and draws the window frames in the shell's colors. With another config, see [Using it with ShojiWM](docs/usage.md#using-it-with-shojiwm).

## Documentation

- [Features](docs/features.md): everything the shell does, part by part.
- [Usage](docs/usage.md): running it, ShojiWM integration, commands and settings.
- [Development](docs/development.md): building against a local AntiWebUI, offscreen previews and CPU reports.
- [Glossary](docs/glossary.md): the bar, islands, panels, placements and shell surfaces' shared language.

name: pine
description: a reactive harness for agents
readme: ```bash npm install -g @pmndrs/pine ``` ### PINE makes AI reactive Most harnesses just do input chat: "Do this do that". And maybe a scheduler: "Do it tomorrow". In PINE agents react to any stimuli. From watching folders, commands, websites, ftp endpoints, webhooks, to any other event source. You can hook them up and let them react to and operate your physical devices in the house, or digital assets. PINE of course also handles regular chat, coding, tasks and orchestration. Agents carry memory and so on. All the basic stuff is in there, too. ### Some design choices - **Event-driven architecture:** Agents subscribe to events and react. An event source is just a `*.ts` service with a schema. Tell the agent what you want and they subscribe: "Watch ~/documents/scans, for every new file: extract summaries and payment details, if present" - **No configs:** Tell the main agent what you want. It configures PINE, creates agents, MCPs, event sources, skills and schedules through administrative tool calls, never touches user config, never messes it up or breaks it. - **Self-discovery:** A built-in BM25 manual tool lets agents look up any API or internal detail on demand, without carrying docs in context. - **A CLI that feels like a desktop app:** Tabs, buttons, scroll regions, inline images and video, and drag-and-drop with thumbnails. Works in Kitty-protocol terminals like Ghostty, with fallbacks for older ones. - **Built in:** Computer use (macOS), web browsing, coding tools, diffs and git, undo, plan mode and goals (`/goal` keeps an agent working until it is done). - **Orchestration:** Agents can delegate, create sub-agents in parallel. A pinned tab simply persists an agent and its task. Name it, give it instructions, chat with it or subscribe it to events. > [!IMPORTA

readme:
# hao-patcher hao-patcher builds disk images of **macOS 27 (Golden Gate) for Intel x86_64 Macs**. The current build is macOS 27.2.1 (26B131). macOS 27 does not support Intel Macs, so the image is built in layers: Golden Gate's own System and Data, the Intel kernel extensions, drivers and boot files macOS 26 (Tahoe) still ships, legacy hardware support from OpenCore Legacy Patcher, a set of compatibility fixes, and [hao-runtime](https://github.com/lythka/hao-runtime), which runs Golden Gate's ARM-only programs on the Intel CPU. ![macOS 27.2.1 on a 2012 MacBook Pro: About This Mac, Control Center and widgets](docs/images/desktop-intel.jpg) [Gallery](docs/gallery.md) · [Progress](docs/progress.md) · [Building](docs/building.md) · [Buy me a coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/lythka) ### Accelerated Metal on the Intel HD 4000 Maps draws its satellite view and 3D buildings with Apple's shader libraries, repaired so the HD 4000's legacy Metal compiler accepts them ([cache/metallib](cache/metallib)). Weather's maps need argument buffers and ASTC textures, which that legacy stack lacks; hao-patcher adds both to the shader compiler and the driver ([tools/metal-argbuf](tools/metal-argbuf)):

More in the [gallery](docs/gallery.md): Safari and YouTube, the wind and air-quality maps, WebGPU and SceneKit. ## Status Experimental. Developed and tested on a 2012 13-inch MacBook Pro (MacBookPro9,2: Ivy Bridge, Intel HD 4000); other Intel Macs are untested. Tested with macOS 27.2.1 (26B131). | Area | What works | |---|---| | Startup | Screen on about 45 s after the kernel starts; Setup Assistant, account creation, automatic login | | Desktop | Menu bar, Dock, Finder, Liquid Glass, login window, lock screen | | Graphics | Accelerate

name: deepseek-v3-jax
description: DeepSeek V3 (MLA, DeepSeekMoE, aux-loss-free balancing, MTP) in 190 lines of pure JAX, trained on a MacBook Air. Write-up: vaibhaav.in/writing/deepseek-v3-jax
readme:
# DeepSeek V3 in pure JAX

The architecture from the [DeepSeek-V3 technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19437) in **190 lines of pure JAX**, pretrained from scratch on a MacBook Air on public-domain detective fiction.

No Flax, no Equinox, no PyTorch. Params are plain dicts of arrays and every part of the model is a function you can read top to bottom in [`deepseek_v3.py`](deepseek_v3.py).

**Read the write-up:** [DeepSeek V3 in 190 lines of pure JAX](https://vaibhaav.in/writing/deepseek-v3-jax/), with diagrams, the code explained piece by piece, and the results.

![The whole model: 36.2M parameters, 13.6M used per token](post/diagrams/01-whole-model-clean.png)

## What's in the 190 lines

| Idea from the paper | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) | Caches one small latent per token instead of full keys and values: **480 → 144** numbers per token per layer here | `mla`, `init_cache` |
| Decoupled RoPE | One rotary key shared by all heads, kept outside the compressed latent | `rope`, `apply_rope`, `mla` |
| DeepSeekMoE | 1 shared expert that always runs + 16 routed experts, top-4 per token | `route`, `moe` |
| Auxiliary-loss-free balancing | A per-expert bias nudges routing toward idle experts; it changes *which* experts are picked, not their weights | `update_bias`, `route` |
| Sequence-wise balance loss | The small complementary loss from the paper (α = 1e-4) | `seq_balance_loss` |
| Multi-token prediction (MTP) | An extra module also predicts the token after next, weighted λ = 0.3 in the loss | `forward`, `loss_fn` |
| Training and generation | bf16 compute on f32 master weights; prefill + decode with the MLA cache | `make_train_step`, `generate` |

## Results

One run of the default config on a MacBook Air M5 (24 GB):

| | |
|---|---|
| Model | 36.2M parameters, 13.6M active per token |
| Data | 207 books, 21.7M training tokens (Hammett repeated 3×); validation is held-out crime fiction |
| Training | 12,000 steps, ~98

name: borland-reborn
description: Borland's DOS compilers, recovered as source that rebuilds the original binaries byte for byte. First up: Borland C++ 2.0's BCC.EXE.
readme:
# borland-reborn

**Borland's DOS compilers, rebuilt from their own binaries.**

This repository recovers the source code of classic Borland compilers from the published
executables, so that the recovered C and assembly rebuild each executable **byte for byte**
with the original Borland toolchain. Then it makes that source readable: real names, named
record fields, comments on every file, and notes on what the compiler does and where it goes
wrong.

| Directory | Program | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [`bcc20/`](bcc20/) | **Borland C++ 2.0** (1991), `BCC.EXE`, the command-line compiler | Complete: rebuilds byte-identical (SHA-256 `dd5744b9...`) |
| [`cpp20/`](cpp20/) | **Borland C++ 2.0** (1991), `CPP.EXE`, the standalone preprocessor | Complete: rebuilds byte-identical (SHA-256 `39879c60...`) |
| [`bcc20-port/`](bcc20-port/) | `BCC.EXE` as a native compiler and library, for decompiling Borland-built games | Complete: every function checked against BCC.EXE; 1874 of 1880 corpus compiles identical; native binaries and a library |

More Borland and Turbo versions will join as further top-level directories, sharing the
[`scripts/`](scripts/) and the [Exhume](https://github.com/abedegno/Exhume) build tools.

## Borland C++ 2.0 at a glance

- **298 sources** in 15 subsystem directories: 265 C files (Borland C++ 2.0 and Turbo C 2.01)
  and 33 hand-written TASM modules. The original's own split into compiled C and hand-written
  assembly is kept: assembly was never forced into C, and compiled code was never left as
  assembly.
- **Every name is recovered or descriptive**: about 3,100 functions, globals and labels, 300
  record fields (`src/include/FIELDS.H`), 40 record layouts (`src/include/RECORDS.H`),
  message, token, type-kind and operator constants.
- **Every file is documented**: a role line, an overview and function comments
  (about 10,000 lines of comments), with [a source map](bcc20/docs/SOURCE-MAP.md) and
  [how the compiler is organised](bcc20/docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md).
